core_meaning.short_meaning: Flowing grace, easy generosity; early companion Suwaybit ibn Harmalah.
core_meaning.primary_meaning: Suwaybit (سُوَيْبِط) is an authentic Arabic masculine given name meaning 'flowing grace', 'generous nature', or 'smooth and gentle spirit'. In Islamic history, it is the renowned name of Suwaybit ibn Harmalah al-Qurashi, an early Meccan convert from Banu Abd al-Dar who migrated to Abyssinia and Medina, and fought at the Battle of Badr.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: Diminutive of sabiṭ (smooth, unknotted, flowing easily and generously), denoting good nature, openheartedness, and gentle kindness.
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: The root s-b-ṭ denotes flowing smoothly, generosity, and abundant ease. Suwaybit ibn Harmalah was among the early adherents of Islam in Mecca who endured persecution and joined the migration to Abyssinia. He was among the honored 313 warriors who stood at Badr with the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, recognized for his cheerful demeanor and steadfast devotion.
